column1: # gene_host_context.tsv -- is a resistance gene INTRINSIC or ACQUIRED for the organism it was found with?
# Seeded from the NCBI Reference Gene Catalog 2026-08-07.1, then curated by hand against the
# literature. Every PMID here has been resolved through NCBI E-utilities and its title read
#   intrinsic              the organism carries this gene chromosomally as a species trait; its
#                          presence is expected and is NOT evidence of acquired resistance
#   acquired               horizontally acquired (plasmid, transposon, integron, ICE)
#   not_expected_in_taxon  no described association between this gene and this organism; on a
#                          low-biomass tNGS library this is more consistent with off-target
#                          mapping, index hopping or reagent contamination than with true carriage
#   undetermined           not adjudicated -- either uncurated, or the evidence does not settle it.
#                          NEVER a silent default: these are printed in a REVIEW: block.
# RESOLUTION: most specific wins -- a species row beats a genus row beats a '*' family default.
# There are deliberately NO '*' rows in this file. A family-wide 'acquired' default would label
# blaTEM-on-Bartonella as acquired resistance, which is exactly the error this table exists to
# prevent. An uncurated combination must surface as undetermined, not as a guess.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the detection pipeline is ResFinder, a catalogue of *acquired* genes. Read
# naively the gene sheet implies every hit is acquired resistance. For blaACT in Enterobacter,
# blaSRT in Serratia, blaCKO in Citrobacter koseri, fosA across the Enterobacteriaceae and lsa(A)
# in Enterococcus faecalis that is wrong -- they are chromosomal genes the species always carries.
# Columns are TAB separated. Notes must not contain a literal tab.
